data.content_ref: inline:{"analogy":null,"claim":"Resilience to correlated failure is determined by causal firebreaks in network topology, not by scale or operational independence: a decentralized network is more resilient only if its topology is organized to prevent cascade propagation.","counterconditions":[{"case":"The decentralized network's topology has no causal firebreaks and relies on shared infrastructure","checker_spec":null,"eval":"observation"},{"case":"The large service has no internal firebreaks and fails as a monolith","checker_spec":null,"eval":"observation"},{"case":"Causal firebreaks are necessary but not sufficient, and some other factor dominates resilience","checker_spec":null,"eval":"observation"}],"definitions":[],"derivation":[],"formalization_refs":[],"mechanism":"Correlated failure propagates through shared dependencies (power grids, network backbones, common software libraries). A decentralized network reduces correlated failure risk only if its topology includes causal firebreaks\u2014points where failure propagation is blocked. Scale and operational independence are neither necessary nor sufficient: a decentralized network with dense interdependencies can be more fragile than a large service with internal firebreaks, and a large service with poor internal isolation can be more fragile than a decentralized network with natural firebreaks. The distinguishing evidence is whether the topology contains verifiable causal firebreaks, not whether operators are nominally independent.","premises":[],"schema":"deepreason-reasoning-envelope-v1","scope":{"covers":[],"excludes":[]},"simulation_refs":[],"uncertainties":[]}
